blocks.text: The UI submits a prompt to a Generate API that returns a job id. A JobStatus poller (or SSE stream) updates the UI until completion. When done, the image is served from object storage/CDN.

Boundary checks:
- One accepted asynchronous job lifecycle.
- Separation between local view state and versioned job updates.
- Safe asset metadata, placeholder, URL, and media-failure states behind an abstract job/asset contract.
- Resume from the stored status URL after reload.

blocks.title: MVP lifecycle decisions
items: Use a job id to track progress.
Show a loading state until the job is done.
Persist job metadata so history loads fast.
Keep the MVP flow simple and reliable.

blocks.title: Generation architecture failure patterns
items: Blocking the UI until the image returns.
No way to recover if the app reloads mid-job.
Hard-coding image data into the API response.
No clear separation between job state and UI.

steps.title: 1. Submit prompt
steps.text: Before transport begins, store the create idempotency key and prompt snapshot. POST /api/images/generations returns 202 Accepted, a Location status URL, job ID, and initial version; only then can the pending command link to the job.

steps.title: 2. Track status
steps.text: Poll or stream job updates until status=done.

steps.title: 3. Render result
steps.text: When done, show the image from CDN and update history.

steps.title: 4. Handle failures
steps.text: If status=failed, preserve the prompt and expose the versioned retry command.

items.label: Async control
items.helperText: Simple polling or SSE works for MVP.

items.label: UX focus
items.helperText: Users know the job is running.

blocks.title: Asynchronous job boundary
blocks.text: For an MVP, simplicity wins. A single job flow with solid error handling and a clear loading state is better than a complex UI that is hard to ship in two weeks.
Worked example: create response is lost, then cancel races completion
The user submits once but the 202 response is lost. Retrying must recover the same job instead of creating a duplicate. Later, a cancel command races the job reaching done.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough
rows: Store idempotency key k1 and pending prompt snapshot.
The UI shows submitting without inventing a job ID.
One intent has one command identity.
Retry k1 rather than creating k2.
The UI remains uncertain but recoverable.
Network uncertainty does not duplicate work.
Normalize job j7 version 2 with indeterminate progress.
Apply the newer unique authoritative version; done may beat an earlier cancelling state.
Render the image or confirmed cancellation with one explanation.
Unique monotonic job versions define order; contradictory equal versions trigger a status refetch.
